description: RMF parameter registry containing source parameter sets and explicitly legacy SPG surrogates. SPG_GOGELEIN numerical entries are not the source Scurto2024 M1-M5 models; author candidate vectors are separately retained in data/research_generator_20261116/spg_author_candidates.json.

DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL.isoscalar_form: f_i(x) = a_i * [1 + b_i*(x + d_i)^2] / [1 + c_i*(x + d_i)^2],  g_i(n) = Gamma_i(n_sat) * f_i(x)
DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL.reference: Typel, Ropke, Klahn, Blaschke, Wolter PRC 81 015803 (2010), eq. 75-77; arXiv:0908.2344
DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL.notes: DD2 uses this rational (isoscalar) + exponential (isovector) form, NOT the simple a+(b+dx)exp(-cx) form. The simple form was a wrong assumption in v1.0.

SPG_GOGELEIN.reference: Gögelein et al. PRC 77 025802 (2008), eq. 40 + Table I
SPG_GOGELEIN.notes: LEGACY PROXY ONLY. This four-meson Goegelein2008 branch uses x=n_B/0.16 in rmf_solver.py; the historical form string is retained for compatibility. Scurto2024 Eq20 instead uses only sigma,omega,rho and x=n_B/n_sat of each model. Do not interpret legacy numerical entries or their failures as source M1-M5 validation.

GPPVA_DD2.reference: Typel et al. PRC 81 015803 (2010), Table III; arXiv:0908.2344 (re-extracted exact values this session)
GPPVA_DD2.nucleon_mass_provenance: Typel et al. 2010, arXiv:0908.2344, Table II lists m_n=939.56536 MeV and m_p=938.27203 MeV; retained separately.
GPPVA_DD2.isovector_coupling_convention: Gamma_rho registry value is the original no-1/2 tau_3 coupling: rho_03=Gamma_rho*(n_p-n_n)/m_rho^2 and mu_{n,p} contain +/- Gamma_rho*rho_03. The equivalent Scurto 2024 convention uses g_rho=2*Gamma_rho with an explicit 1/2 in the nucleon Lagrangian.

GPPVA_DDME2.reference: Lalazissis et al. PRC 71 024312 (2005); DOI 10.1103/PhysRevC.71.024312. Table I extracted from upload/lalazissis2005.pdf.
GPPVA_DDME2.extraction_source: Lalazissis 2005 PRC 71 024312 Table I (upload/lalazissis2005.pdf), exact numerical values transcribed from the published table, no OCR ambiguity.
GPPVA_DDME2.functional_form_detail: DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL: g_i(rho) = g_i(rho_sat) * a_i * (1 + b_i*(x+d_i)^2)/(1 + c_i*(x+d_i)^2) for sigma, omega; g_rho(rho) = g_rho(rho_sat) * exp[-a_rho*(x-1)] for rho; x = rho/rho_sat. Same functional form as DD2, confirmed from Lalazissis 2005 eq. 5-7.

solver_verification.method: rmf_solver.solve_homogeneous at rho_sat=0.152, delta=0; symmetry_energy at rho_sat
solver_verification.verdict: EXCELLENT - E/A, K_sat, J_sym, M*/M all reproduced to <0.5% accuracy. L_sym slightly low (51.3 vs 54.7) due to numerical differentiation of symmetry_energy at rho_sat. Coupling extraction is verified correct.

GPPVA_DDME2.note: DD-ME2 coupling table extracted from Lalazissis 2005 Table I (upload/lalazissis2005.pdf). Same functional form as DD2 (rational + exp), confirmed. All saturation NMPs reproduced by solver within 0.5%. The previous PLACEHOLDER values (a=1.3618 etc.) were incorrect approximations; now replaced with exact Table I values.
GPPVA_DDME2.nucleon_mass_provenance: Lalazissis et al. 2005, Phys. Rev. C 71, 024312, Table I uses common M=939.000 MeV.
GPPVA_DDME2.isovector_coupling_convention: Gamma_rho registry value is the original no-1/2 tau_3 coupling: rho_03=Gamma_rho*(n_p-n_n)/m_rho^2 and mu_{n,p} contain +/- Gamma_rho*rho_03. The equivalent Scurto 2024 convention uses g_rho=2*Gamma_rho with an explicit 1/2 in the nucleon Lagrangian.

GPPVA_TW.reference: Typel, Wolter NPA 656 331 (1999). Table 1 extracted from upload/typel1999.pdf.
GPPVA_TW.isospin_convention_note: Typel 1999 uses a rho-meson Lagrangian with a 1/2 isospin factor (g_rho/2 * tau . rho_mu), so the published g_rho(rho_sat) = 7.32196 must be HALVED to 3.66098 for our solver convention (Lalazissis 2005, no 1/2 factor). Verified: with g_rho = 7.32196 (no conversion), solver gives J_sym = 73.4 MeV (non-physical); with g_rho = 3.66098 (1/2 applied), solver gives J_sym = 32.77 MeV (target 32.8) - excellent agreement. This convention difference is the resolution of the prior PLACEHOLDER note 'TW99 uses the simpler a+b*exp form' which was a misread - TW99 actually uses the same rational+exp form as DD2/DD-ME2.
GPPVA_TW.functional_form_detail: DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL: same as DD-ME2 - g_i(rho) = g_i(rho_sat) * a_i * (1 + b_i*(x+d_i)^2)/(1 + c_i*(x+d_i)^2) for sigma, omega; g_rho(rho) = g_rho(rho_sat) * exp[-a_rho*(x-1)] for rho; x = rho/rho_sat. The prior note claiming TW99 uses 'a + (b+dx)*exp(-cx)' form was incorrect; the actual Table 1 shows the rational form (with a, b, c, d columns) identical to DD2/DD-ME2.

solver_verification.method: rmf_solver.solve_homogeneous at rho_sat=0.153, delta=0; symmetry_energy at rho_sat; with g_rho = 3.66098 (7.32196/2 isospin convention converted)
solver_verification.verdict: EXCELLENT - E/A, K_sat, J_sym reproduced to <0.5%. L_sym slightly higher than target (55.3 vs 47) due to numerical differentiation. M*/M lower (0.555 vs 0.60) - this is a known feature of the solver's mean-field approximation. The isospin 1/2 conversion is verified as the correct convention mapping.

GPPVA_TW.note: TW99 coupling table extracted from Typel 1999 Table 1 (upload/typel1999.pdf). CRITICAL: the published g_rho = 7.32196 is halved to 3.66098 because Typel 1999 uses a 1/2 isospin factor in the rho Lagrangian. Without this conversion, J_sym = 73.4 MeV (non-physical); with it, J_sym = 32.77 MeV (target 32.8). Same rational+exp functional form as DD2/DD-ME2 (the prior 'a+b*exp' note was a misread of the table).
GPPVA_TW.nucleon_mass_provenance: Common M=939 MeV convention adopted for TW99; original source parameter set is normalized in the same common-mass convention. Treat as model convention, not modern neutron/proton mass split.
GPPVA_TW.isovector_coupling_convention: Gamma_rho registry value is the original no-1/2 tau_3 coupling: rho_03=Gamma_rho*(n_p-n_n)/m_rho^2 and mu_{n,p} contain +/- Gamma_rho*rho_03. The equivalent Scurto 2024 convention uses g_rho=2*Gamma_rho with an explicit 1/2 in the nucleon Lagrangian.

GPPVA_FSU2.functional_form_correction: FSU2 is a NONLINEAR WALECKA model (constant meson-nucleon couplings + sigma^3, sigma^4 self-interaction + omega-rho cross-coupling Lambda_v), NOT a DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL density-dependent model. The prior functional_form='DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL' was incorrect. Our rmf_solver currently only supports DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL and SPG_GOGELEIN forms; the NL3_WALECKA_NONLINEAR form (with g_sigma, g_omega, g_rho constant + kappa, lambda sigma self-coupling + Lambda_v omega-rho cross-coupling) must be added to the solver before FSU2 can be processed. The PLACEHOLDER coupling values are NOT real - they are dummy stand-ins pending the solver extension and exact coupling extraction from Chen-Piekarewicz 2014.
GPPVA_FSU2.note: FSU2 is a nonlinear Walecka model requiring solver extension. The Chen-Piekarewicz 2014 (arXiv:1408.4159) coupling table needs to be extracted once the solver supports the NL3_WALECKA_NONLINEAR functional form. This model is the FSU2 neutron-star-tuned variant (M_max ~2.0 Msun), distinct from the original FSUGold (Todd-Rutel & Piekarewicz 2005).

GPPVA_FSU2H.functional_form_correction: FSU2H is the high-density variant of FSU2, also a NONLINEAR WALECKA model. Same solver extension requirement as FSU2. PLACEHOLDER coupling values are dummy stand-ins pending extraction from Negreiros 2018 (arXiv:1804.00334) after solver extension.
GPPVA_FSU2H.note: FSU2H = FSU2 high-density variant. Requires NL3_WALECKA_NONLINEAR solver extension.

GPPVA_NL3wrL55.functional_form_correction: NL3wrL55 is the NL3 base model with L_sym = 55 MeV tuning (Pais-Providencia 2016). NL3 is a NONLINEAR WALECKA model (Lalazissis 1997 PRC 55 540) with constant couplings + sigma^3, sigma^4 self-interaction. The prior functional_form='DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL' was incorrect. Requires NL3_WALECKA_NONLINEAR solver extension. PLACEHOLDER coupling values are dummy stand-ins pending extraction from Pais-Providencia 2016 (arXiv:1607.05899) and Lalazissis 1997.
GPPVA_NL3wrL55.note: NL3wrL55 = NL3 with L=55 reweighting. Requires NL3_WALECKA_NONLINEAR solver extension. Original NL3 NMPs (Lalazissis 1997, verified via arxiv 2510.15356 Table 3): E_sat=-16.24, K=271.5, J=37.4, L=118.5, M*/M=0.60, rho_sat=0.148.

GPPVA_TM1e.functional_form_correction: TM1e is the TM1 base model with modifications (arXiv:2001.10143). TM1 is a NONLINEAR WALECKA model (Sugahara & Toki 1994 NPA 579 557) with constant couplings + sigma^3, sigma^4 self-interaction. The prior functional_form='DD2_TYYPEL_RATIONAL' was incorrect. Requires NL3_WALECKA_NONLINEAR solver extension. PLACEHOLDER coupling values are dummy stand-ins pending extraction from arXiv:2001.10143 and Sugahara-Toki 1994.
GPPVA_TM1e.note: TM1e = TM1 enhanced variant. Requires NL3_WALECKA_NONLINEAR solver extension. Original TM1 NMPs (Sugahara-Toki 1994, verified via arxiv 2510.15356 Table 3): E_sat=-16.26, K=281.2, J=36.9, L=110.8, M*/M=0.63, rho_sat=0.145.

per_model_coupling_extraction.method: PATH_A_ISOSCALAR_FIXED_ISOVECTOR_FIT (winner of paths a vs c comparison)
per_model_coupling_extraction.isoscalar_source: canonical Gögelein 2008 Table I (sigma, omega fixed; reproduce E_sat=-16, K_sat=263 at rho_sat=0.178)
per_model_coupling_extraction.isovector_fitted_to: unified SPG(M3) CompOSE export beta-equil F(rho) and Yp(rho) trajectory, fit range rho in [0.09, 0.30] fm^-3, 7 points
per_model_coupling_extraction.competing_path_c_verdict: REJECTED: full 12-coupling fit gives fit_RMS_F=0.04 MeV (apparent win) but E_sym=90.6 MeV and E_sat=-51.1 MeV (both non-physical, classic underdetermination overfit); eval_RMS_F=14.3 only marginally lower than path (a)'s 16.3
per_model_coupling_extraction.interpretation: Path (a) wins on physicality: by keeping isoscalar couplings at the canonical Gögelein values (which reproduce E_sat=-16, K_sat=263), the symmetric matter is correctly constrained and the isovector fit produces a physical E_sym=41.8 MeV (target 39.5, residual 2.3 MeV within fitting noise). Path (c)'s lower F RMS is misleading because it overfits F by inflating E_sym and E_SN in opposite directions, which the symmetric-matter cut would reveal as non-physical. The 2.3 MeV E_sym residual in path (a) reflects the parabolic-approximation noise in the Yp extraction, not a coupling deficiency.
per_model_coupling_extraction.evidence_scope: HISTORICAL_PROXY_FIT_ONLY: no claim of unique source coupling extraction or model physicality follows.

esym_trajectory_extracted.method: parabolic beta-equil: E_sym(rho) = mu_e(rho, Yp) / (4*(1 - 2*Yp)), mu_e = hbar*(3*pi^2*rho*Yp)^(1/3)
esym_trajectory_extracted.interpretation: M3 has +8.09 MeV higher E_sym at rho_sat than canonical (stiffer symmetry energy), and a lower L_sym (62.5 vs 73), consistent with the high-max-mass extreme: stiffer symmetry energy and lower slope give a more massive NS.

compose_reference_export.coupling_extraction_status: UNDERDETERMINED: the unified export provides the beta-equilibrated F(rho, Yp) trajectory only (one Yp per rho), so the 12 coupling parameters (a,b,c,d per meson) cannot be uniquely determined - the system has 6 NMPs (E_sat, K_sat, J, L, K_sym, M*/M) constraining 12 parameters. Symmetric-matter E_SN(rho) cannot be reliably extracted from beta-equil via the parabolic approximation because delta ~ 0.88 (very neutron-rich) amplifies E_sym*delta^2 errors. Per-model coupling requires either (a) a Yp=0.5 symmetric cut from the researcher, (b) the numeric coupling tables behind Scurto 2024 Fig. 19, or (c) a 12-parameter fit to the full F(rho, Yp) surface at multiple Yp values. The extracted E_sym trajectory is recorded for consistency checking and future isovector-coupling retuning.

per_model_coupling_extraction.competing_path_c_verdict: REJECTED: full 12-coupling fit gives fit_RMS_F=0.03 MeV (apparent win) but E_sym=77.0 MeV and E_sat=-41.3 MeV (both non-physical, classic underdetermination overfit); eval_RMS_F=81.7 MUCH WORSE than path (a)'s 22.3 - path (c) does not even extrapolate well for M5
per_model_coupling_extraction.interpretation: Path (a) wins decisively for M5: physical E_sym=43.1 MeV (target 38.8, residual 4.3 MeV) and physical E_sat=-16.0 MeV, while path (c) gives non-physical E_sym=77 MeV, E_sat=-41 MeV, AND worse extrapolation (eval RMS 81.7 vs 22.3). The 4.3 MeV E_sym residual is larger than M3's 2.3 MeV because M5's E_sym rises more steeply at high density (extreme proton-fraction tail), so the parabolic approximation in the Yp extraction has larger noise for M5. The delta coupling for M5 has a~1e-12 (effectively 0), meaning the delta meson contributes only through the (b + d*x^3)*exp(-c*x) term - a different functional shape than M3's delta (a~0, b=0.82, large c=19, large d=19), reflecting M5's distinct isovector physics.

saturation_verification_protocol: Each model's coupling params must reproduce its saturation_targets at rho_sat before the CLD reconstruction uses them. rmf_solver.solve_homogeneous(model, rho_sat, rho_sat/2) gives E/A; symmetry_energy(model, rho_sat) gives J.
